title: Topical mastery and correction
learning_outcomes: Complete a rising-difficulty Kinematics set using disciplined method selection.
Diagnose errors by cause and write transferable correction rules.
Retry missed skills after a delay and check for repeated errors.
prior_knowledge_summary: Students can choose representations and isolate Kinematics leaves in mixed questions.
Students can solve definitions, graphs, equations, free fall and ideal projectile motion.
Students can preserve dependencies, signs and units.
new_learning: A repeatable timed-attempt, diagnosis, correction and delayed-retry cycle.
Error classification by model, sign, graph, algebra, unit and interpretation.
Targeted prevention rules that transfer across Kinematics contexts.
not_yet_taught: Statistical claims about mastery beyond this lesson's evidence.
knowledge_boundary: No new content is introduced. The lesson consolidates all Kinematics outcomes through diagnosis and correction.

evidence_basis.canonical_audit: Programmatically read all 79 mapped enrichment records and their indexed part IDs, plus controlled registries; sampled whole canonical questions, official mark schemes and every relevant diagram form used in the lesson.
evidence_basis.mapping_scope_note: The full enrichment files contain many non-Kinematics leaves. Only part_ids explicitly selected by the Kinematics evidence index are in scope.

blocks.title: A wrong answer can be useful
body: Two students score 6 out of 10. One writes 'careless' beside every error. The other labels each miss: model, sign, graph, algebra, unit or interpretation. Who is more likely to improve on the retry? Predict why.
A score tells you how much went wrong. An error code tells you what to change. This lesson turns a timed Kinematics set into a correction cycle.

blocks.title: Use a fixed first-minute routine
body: Before calculating, mark the target, model, positive direction, known quantities and representation. Estimate the sign and rough size. This small setup prevents many expensive errors.
Definitions must stay exact: displacement is distance in a specified direction from a point; velocity is rate of change of displacement; acceleration is rate of change of velocity.

definitions.display: distance in a specified direction from a point

blocks.title: Correct the method, not only the number
body: A runner changes velocity from +5.0 m s^-1 to -1.0 m s^-1 in 2.0 s. Writing 2.0 m s^-2 from speed change misses direction. The correct change is -1.0 - 5.0 = -6.0 m s^-1, so a = -3.0 m s^-2.
The correction note is: 'I subtracted speeds instead of signed velocities. Next time I write v - u before using a = Δv/Δt.' That rule transfers to a new question.

blocks.title: Audit graphs and equations differently
body: For a graph, check axes, units, scale, gradient, signed area, intercepts and whether a curve or straight line matches the motion. For equations, check constant acceleration, one interval, signs, units and significant figures.
A correct formula with inconsistent signs is not a correct model. A neat graph with the wrong initial value is not a correct representation.

figure.brief: Teacher-sketch visual for graph precision checklist with terse labels and check marks.
figure.alt_text: A teaching sketch of graph precision checklist.

blocks.title: More practice is not always better practice
body: It feels productive to repeat ten similar questions immediately. That can train the same hidden error. First diagnose, then write one correction rule, then retry a changed question after a delay.
Sort errors by cause, not by topic heading. A sign error can appear in free fall, graph area and projectile impact. One strong correction rule can repair all three.

blocks.title: Motion language and signs
body: Distance is the total path length. Displacement is distance in a specified direction from a point.
Speed describes how quickly distance changes. Velocity is rate of change of displacement.

Acceleration is rate of change of velocity. A negative velocity means motion in the negative direction. A negative acceleration means acceleration points in that direction, not automatically that the object slows.
Before calculating, draw a positive axis and attach signs to every vector quantity.

blocks.title: Read and build motion graphs
body: On a displacement-time graph, gradient gives velocity. A horizontal section means zero velocity.
On a velocity-time graph, gradient gives acceleration and signed area gives displacement. Area below the time axis is negative displacement.
For distance from a velocity-time graph, add the magnitudes of the areas. For displacement, add signed areas.
When constructing a graph, label axes and units, plot boundary values, use straight lines only for constant gradient, and preserve sign changes.

blocks.title: Choose and check constant-acceleration equations
body: Use the equations only for straight-line motion with constant acceleration. Make a u-v-a-s-t snapshot for one interval.
Select the equation containing the target and knowns but not an unwanted unknown. Rearrange with symbols, substitute signed values with units, then interpret the sign.
For linked stages, the final state of one stage is the initial state of the next. Reverse solving starts from the known later boundary.
Check by dimensions, scale, direction and an independent route such as average velocity or a second equation.

blocks.title: Vertical motion and measuring g
body: In free fall without air resistance, every object has the same downward acceleration g, regardless of mass.
For upward-positive motion, a = -g throughout ascent, turning point and descent. At the top v = 0 but acceleration remains -g.
A launch from above ground needs the displacement from launch to ground, with its sign, when finding total flight time.
To measure g from release at rest, plot s against t^2. The gradient is g/2. Repeats, a best-fit line and intercept inspection help diagnose uncertainty.

blocks.title: Projectile chain
body: Resolve launch velocity into horizontal and vertical components. Horizontal velocity stays constant when air resistance is negligible; vertical acceleration is downward g.
Use vertical displacement to find flight time. Use that same time horizontally to find range.
Find final vertical velocity with signs, then combine it with horizontal velocity using Pythagoras for speed and trigonometry for direction.
For unequal levels, do not use same-level symmetry. Put the actual signed vertical displacement into the vertical equation.

blocks.title: Represent, isolate, correct and retry
body: Choose words for a qualitative state, a graph for a pattern over time, and an equation for an exact value under a valid model.
Inside a mixed-topic chain, box the Kinematics leaf. Keep context that sets boundaries and direction, but set aside later-topic data until it is needed.
When an answer fails, label the error: model, sign, graph, algebra, unit, arithmetic or interpretation. Correct the method and write one prevention rule.
Retry the same skill after a delay with changed numbers or context. A correct delayed route is stronger evidence than copying a correction immediately.

blocks.title: The mastery loop
body: Attempt under time. Mark by criteria. Classify every lost mark. Rework without looking at the answer. Write a prevention rule. Retry a changed item later. Track whether the same error returns.
Mastery means choosing a valid model, showing enough working, controlling signs and units, drawing precise graphs and checking whether the final answer makes physical sense.

concepts_taught: Mastery uses a timed attempt, criteria-based marking, error diagnosis, correction rule and delayed retry.
Errors should be classified by cause across contexts.
Physical plausibility, signs, units and representation precision are final checks.
misconceptions_addressed: A score identifies what to improve.
Repeating similar questions immediately guarantees correction.
A correct formula guarantees a correct answer.
skills_students_can_now_use: Complete and audit a topical Kinematics set.
Classify model, sign, graph, algebra, unit and interpretation errors.
Plan and evaluate a delayed retry.
next_lesson_can_assume: Students have completed the Kinematics pathway and a verified mastery cycle.
next_lesson_must_not_assume: Students will retain mastery without later spaced retrieval.
Students know content beyond the Kinematics scope.
